program_overview.title: Complete Generative AI Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: The modern AI stack, engineered rather than prompted at: LLMs understood, RAG built properly, agents shipped with guardrails, in ten honest months.
program_overview.description:
Generative AI created a new engineering discipline in record time, and most courses responded with either hype or screenshots. This masterclass responds with engineering. It starts from zero, Python, the working mathematics, a fast pass through classical ML and neural networks, because LLM engineering without foundations is prompt-guessing with extra steps. Then it goes where the real demand is: transformer architecture understood deeply enough to reason about, LLM APIs across providers, prompt engineering with evaluation harnesses, embeddings and vector search, retrieval-augmented generation built and hardened twice, fine-tuning judgment, open-weight models run locally, and AI agents, architecture, tools, memory and the guardrails that keep them honest.

The production phase is what separates this course from tutorials: application architecture, observability, security against prompt injection, cost control, and a capstone shipped behind an API and defended. What it refuses to fake: training frontier models from scratch, research careers and startup playbooks are mapped honestly as next roads, not sold as weeks.

The pace is real: ten months at two live classes a week plus five to six hours of practice, with two more in hand when needed. Problem sets after every class, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate, with focused revision and a free retest. Real systems, real evaluation, depth over dopamine.

why_this_course.title: Why Generative AI Is an Engineering Discipline Now
paragraphs: The prompt-tips era is over. Companies shipping GenAI in 2026 hire people who can build retrieval that survives messy documents, agents that fail safely, evaluation harnesses that catch regressions, and systems whose costs are understood before the invoice arrives. That is engineering, and it is teachable.

This masterclass builds it in the honest order: foundations first, because transformer intuition without mathematics is superstition; then the LLM core, retrieval and agents, each with evaluation built in; then production, observability, security and cost, the layer that separates demos from systems.

It ends the way real learning should: a capstone system deployed and defended, a final exam that decides the certificate, and a truthful map of the roads beyond, from enterprise agents to deep ML research.
highlights: 40 teaching weeks from Python to a deployed GenAI capstone
RAG built and hardened twice, agents with guardrails, fine-tuning judgment
Provider-agnostic: frontier APIs and open-weight local models
Evaluation harnesses and security treated as core skills

faqs.question: What does this generative AI course actually teach?
faqs.answer: The modern AI engineering stack, from zero: Python and working mathematics, honest ML basics, then transformers understood in depth, LLM APIs across providers, prompt engineering with evaluation harnesses, embeddings and vector search, RAG built and then hardened for real documents, AI agents with tools, memory and guardrails, fine-tuning judgment, open-weight models run locally, and production skills: architecture, observability, security and cost control, ending in a deployed capstone.

faqs.question: How long does it take to become good at generative AI?
faqs.answer: Ten months at 2 live classes a week plus 5 to 6 hours of practice, from zero, and that includes the foundations most GenAI courses skip. The course keeps two more months in hand for learners who need them. Weekend prompt courses produce prompt-guessers; this produces engineers, and the difference shows in the first technical interview.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews mix new material with earlier topics deliberately, each phase ends with an exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical GenAI engineering task plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Do I need to know Python or machine learning already?
faqs.answer: No. Phase 1 builds Python, the working mathematics and honest ML basics precisely so that the generative phases rest on understanding rather than copy-paste. Existing developers skip nothing but move faster, and go deeper in the practice work.

faqs.question: Which models and tools does the course use?
faqs.answer: All the ones that matter, by design: frontier APIs (GPT-class, Claude-class, Gemini-class), open-weight models like the Llama family run locally, vector databases, and framework tooling with an honest verdict on when it helps versus native SDKs. The patterns are the syllabus; providers are examples, so the skills survive the next model release.

faqs.question: Does the course cover AI agents?
faqs.answer: As a core phase, not a teaser: agent architecture, tool use, memory, planning, failure modes and the guardrail stack, built into working systems and then hardened in the production phase. Students who want the enterprise low-code layer continue into our Copilot Studio courses; those who want agentic coding continue into Codex and Claude Code.

faqs.question: Will I train my own large language model?
faqs.answer: You will fine-tune and run open-weight models, and understand training deeply enough to reason about it. Training frontier models from scratch costs millions and is honestly mapped as a research-career road, not sold as a course week. What employers actually need, adaptation, retrieval, agents and production judgment, is exactly what the course builds.

faqs.question: What are the fees?
faqs.answer: Group classes are ₹1,499 per month, with 2 live classes a week in batches capped at 10 learners. A mini batch of 3-4 learners is ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. International learners pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.

faqs.question: Can I try a class before enrolling?
faqs.answer: Yes, a free demo class with no commitment: book at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact or message us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161. You will build a small working GenAI piece inside the demo itself.

faqs.question: Are classes live or recorded?
faqs.answer: Live, always: small groups with a real instructor reading your actual code and traces, never pre-recorded videos. GenAI systems fail in quiet, expensive ways; live review is the only honest way to build the judgment that catches them.
